source_text: Sic et cum e diverso statuens prave agere in aliorum iniuriam, vel iniquus quis fuerit, vel crudelis; operatio qua nocet aliis, a nequitia foras proficiscitur, quam intus mala voluntas seminavit et genuit; cum vero deest facultas, per quam in proximos vis secretae voluntatis erumpat, in ipsa tamen sola voluntate, quae aliquid vel boni, vel mali, non impetu brevi, sed cogitatione appetituque patraverit, vel benignitatis est ratio impleta, vel malignitatis.
pass_a_gloss: So also when from the other side, setting to act crookedly unto injury of others, someone has been either unjust or cruel; the operation by which he harms others sets out abroad from the wickedness which inside an evil will sowed and generated; but when the faculty is lacking, through which the force of a secret will may burst upon neighbors, nevertheless in that will alone, which shall have accomplished something either of good or of evil, not by a brief impulse, but by thought and appetite, either the account of kindness has been filled, or of malice.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Likewise, on the opposite side, when someone resolves to act wrongly to others' injury and becomes unjust or cruel, the act by which he harms others comes outward from the wickedness that an evil will sowed and generated within. But when the means are lacking by which the force of the hidden will may break out against one's neighbors, the character of kindness or malice is nevertheless complete in that will alone, when it has accomplished something good or evil not through a brief impulse but through deliberate thought and desire.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
